benchmark_ibov.note: Official Ibovespa level (B3 defines it as a gross total-return index, so cash dividends are already reinvested in the published series). No extra dividend was added. No investor cost.

audit.finding: Primary drawdown near -99% matches a net CAGR near -24% compounded for about 16 years. It is not a cash charge, not a daily charge on the whole book, and not a drawdown taken on the wrong series. Gross and net hold the same shares. The terminal wealth gap matches fee + half-spread + slippage; a touch inside the close is recorded as zero half-spread, so the gap can sit slightly under that sum. Slippage is almost all of the gap. The book is in cash on most rebalances. The few entries invest the whole NAV in one or two names, far above 10% of ADV, so the linear participation model hits its 5000 bps cap. That cost is what the published model charges. A separate bug did inflate the equal-weight small-cap benchmark: replacing the book sold and rebought names that stayed, paying spread and slippage on the whole book every rebalance. Replacement now trades only the weight change. The primary path holds until exit and did not take that round trip.

verdict.note: Aprovado para paper só com custos no retorno, DSR >= 0,95 usando N de todas as variações registradas, e trilha pelo menos tão longa quanto o MinTRL. Isso não autoriza capital.
